summary.title: Blog Writing for Developers
summary.one_liner: Developer-focused advice on why and how to write blogs and docs, covering clarity, voice, a three-part structure, editing, tooling and what to write about.
keywords: how to write a technical blog
tell them what you're going to tell them
what to write about as a developer
takeaways: Write for yourself as a developer, since you are also the reader; aim for clarity first, then calibrate personality to audience.
Use a simple structure: an intro that tells readers why it matters, the article body, and a recap with a next step or call to action.
Start writing early, iterate repeatedly, and use time-boxed breaks such as a Pomodoro timer to get unstuck.
Get a good reviewer and copyeditor, and proofread your work before publishing.
Find topics in developer communities by noting repeated questions, misunderstandings and new trends; avoid growth-driven SEO bait.
summary.summary: Robin Moffatt shares his personal approach to writing for developers, explaining why he writes (sharing information, learning, building credibility) and how he structures posts. He covers three dimensions to balance: clarity, personality/voice, and uniformity of content, and notes how these vary by medium and company. The post also gives practical advice on intros, recaps, iterating on drafts, getting editors and reviewers, his tooling stack, a list of resources, and ideas for choosing topics. It recommends Larry McEnerney's lecture "The Craft of Writing Effectively" as essential viewing.
